summary.business_type: Local financial services — vehicle hire purchase / asset finance, single location, Kathmandu, Nepal. NRB-licensed lender, part of MV Dugar Group.
top_findings: All 13 public routes ship the identical title tag and have no meta description — no title/meta management exists anywhere in the codebase.
No sitemap.xml and no site-owned robots.txt; /sitemap.xml returns the SPA shell with HTTP 200.
Soft 404s: every unknown URL returns HTTP 200 with the SPA shell, creating unlimited indexable duplicates of the homepage.
Zero structured data site-wide — no FinancialService, FAQPage, Organization, Article or BreadcrumbList JSON-LD.
Security headers declared in vercel.json are never applied — the site is served by Cloudflare, which does not read that file.
robots.txt actively blocks GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot and others, making the brand uncitable in AI search.
Homepage transfers 3.79 MB, including a 3000x1975 image rendered at 95x600 px.
quick_wins: Add per-route <title> and <meta name="description"> — React 19 hoists these natively, no new dependency needed.
Ship public/sitemap.xml (12 routes + 7 blog posts) and public/robots.txt with a Sitemap: directive.
Add FAQPage JSON-LD to the homepage — the 5 Q&As are already written and rendered.
Add alt text to the 6 homepage images that lack it, plus loading="lazy" and explicit width/height on all images.
Add Open Graph and Twitter Card tags — every social share currently renders as a blank card.

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: HTTPS enforced, served from Cloudflare edge with a 607 ms TTFB
No redirect chains observed across the 20 URLs crawled
html lang="en" and a correct viewport meta tag are present
Hashed asset filenames enable safe long-term caching

findings.title: No XML sitemap
findings.description: /sitemap.xml returns the SPA shell with HTTP 200 and Content-Type: text/html, not XML. Google has no crawl manifest for the site's 20 URLs.
findings.recommendation: Generate public/sitemap.xml at build time covering the 12 public routes plus the 7 blog slugs from src/data/posts.js, and submit it in Google Search Console.

findings.title: Soft 404s — unknown URLs return HTTP 200
findings.description: Verified: /this-page-does-not-exist-xyz returns HTTP 200 with the SPA shell. The React NotFound component renders, but Google reads a 200 status, so every typo'd or stale URL becomes an indexable duplicate of the homepage.
findings.recommendation: Return a real 404 status for unmatched paths via a Cloudflare Pages Function or 404.html fallback. As interim mitigation, render <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> from the NotFound component.

findings.title: Security headers declared but never applied
findings.description: vercel.json defines CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, but the live response carries none of them. Server: cloudflare, with no Vercel headers present — the deployment platform does not read vercel.json.
findings.recommendation: Port all six headers to a Cloudflare Transform Rule or a public/_headers file, then delete or annotate vercel.json so it is not mistaken for live configuration.

findings.title: /admin is publicly reachable and indexable
findings.description: App.jsx comments the route as a 'hidden admin dashboard', but there is no noindex, no robots disallow, and no server-side gate on the route. Obscurity is not access control.
findings.recommendation: Add Disallow: /admin and noindex as damage limitation, then add real server-side authentication on the backend endpoints the dashboard calls.

findings.title: No site-owned robots.txt
findings.description: robots.txt is Cloudflare's managed default. It allows general crawling but carries no Sitemap: directive and was not authored for this site.
findings.recommendation: Create public/robots.txt with Allow: /, Disallow: /admin, and a Sitemap: directive — carrying the AI-crawler decision forward deliberately.

findings.title: Client-side rendering leaves raw HTML empty
findings.description: Raw HTML is 942 bytes: an empty <div id="root">. All content requires JS execution. Googlebot renders JS on a deferred second pass; Bingbot and most AI crawlers largely do not.
findings.recommendation: Add build-time prerendering (e.g. vite-plugin-prerender) to emit static HTML per route while keeping the existing React code — far cheaper than migrating to Next.js or Remix.

findings.title: No canonical tags on any route
findings.description: Zero canonical tags site-wide. Combined with soft 404s, this leaves the site defenceless against duplicate indexing from ?utm_* parameters, trailing slashes and typo'd paths.
findings.recommendation: Emit a self-referencing <link rel="canonical"> per route from the Seo component.

findings.title: No Cache-Control on HTML; short TTL on immutable assets
findings.description: HTML is served with no Cache-Control header. Content-hashed assets get max-age=14400 (4 hours) despite filenames that can never change.
findings.recommendation: Set max-age=31536000, immutable on hashed assets and an explicit short TTL with revalidation on HTML.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Copy is specific, plainly written and free of finance-industry padding
Service categories break down into concrete asset types with real examples
Homepage FAQ answers genuine borrower questions (down payment, approval time, documents)
A /leadership page with named executives and a /reports page provide real E-E-A-T signals for a regulated lender
Blog offers concrete, quotable guidance such as the 2x income-to-EMI rule of thumb

findings.title: Thin blog content
findings.description: 7 posts totalling roughly 1,444 words of body copy in src/data/posts.js — averaging about 200 words each, with the featured pillar post the longest at around 330. Well below what ranks for competitive terms like 'hire purchase Nepal'.
findings.recommendation: Expand the three highest-intent posts to 1,200-1,800 words with worked examples using real Nepali price points, comparison tables, and internal links to /services and /emi-calculator.

findings.title: No author attribution on YMYL financial content
findings.description: Blog posts carry no byline, author bio or credentials. Google weighs author expertise heavily for financial content. The /leadership page has the people; the posts do not connect to them.
findings.recommendation: Add an author field to each post in posts.js linked to a bio on /leadership, and mark it up with Article + Person schema.

findings.title: Testimonials labelled 'GOOGLE REVIEW' are hardcoded in source
findings.description: Five named testimonials render from static component data rather than from the Google Business Profile. If any are illustrative rather than genuine, the 'GOOGLE REVIEW' label is a Google policy violation and a consumer-protection concern.
findings.recommendation: Verify each testimonial against a real GBP review. If genuine, pull them from the GBP API so they stay current. If not, remove the label. Do not add Review schema until this is settled.

findings.title: No machine-readable publication dates
findings.description: Posts use Bikram Sambat dates ('Asar 26, 2083') — correct for the audience, but there is no ISO datePublished anywhere, so Google cannot assess freshness.
findings.recommendation: Add an ISO datePublished alongside the BS display date. Keep showing BS to readers; give Google ISO in the schema.

findings.title: NRB license claimed without a number
findings.description: 'Licensed by Nepal Rastra Bank' appears on the hero and About page with no license number, and the site publishes no street address or business hours anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Publish the NRB license number next to the claim, a full street address with ward and landmark, and business hours on /contact and in LocalBusiness schema.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Exactly one H1 per page across all routes
Alt text that does exist is well written and descriptive
Main navigation links 8 routes with clean, readable URL slugs

findings.title: One title tag shared across all 13 routes
findings.description: Every route returns <title>Manokamana Hire Purchase</title> — 23 characters, no service or location keywords. Verified by grep: no react-helmet, no document.title writes anywhere in src/.
findings.recommendation: Build a small Seo component using React 19's native metadata hoisting (no new dependency) and set unique titles per route; a full recommended set is in ACTION-PLAN.md.

findings.title: Zero meta descriptions
findings.description: None of the 13 routes has a meta description, so Google fabricates snippets from page text for every result.
findings.recommendation: Add unique 140-160 character descriptions per route via the same Seo component.

findings.title: No Open Graph or Twitter Card tags
findings.description: Zero social meta tags site-wide. Every WhatsApp, Facebook and LinkedIn share renders as a blank grey card — a daily conversion leak for a business that runs on local referral.
findings.recommendation: Add og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url and twitter:card, plus a default 1200x630 OG image.

findings.title: /reports is orphaned from site navigation
findings.description: The /reports route is reachable only by direct URL — it appears in no nav or footer link. For a regulated lender, published financial disclosures are a strong E-E-A-T asset going to waste.
findings.recommendation: Link /reports from the main navigation or footer.

findings.title: Brand-led H1 carries no search keywords
findings.description: The homepage H1 is 'Powering Nepal Through Hire Purchase' — a good brand line but a weak SEO line against what people actually search.
findings.recommendation: Keep the brand line as the visual hero and carry a keyword-bearing phrase such as 'Vehicle Hire Purchase Financing in Nepal' in the H1 or title tag.

findings.title: Heading level skipped on the homepage
findings.description: The homepage jumps H1 to H3 at the 'Driven By Your Ambitions' band before returning to H2.
findings.recommendation: Demote or promote that heading so levels descend without skipping.

findings.title: Zero JSON-LD site-wide
findings.description: No structured data on any page. For an NRB-licensed local lender this is the single biggest missed opportunity — FinancialService/LocalBusiness, FAQPage, Organization, Article, BreadcrumbList, Service and JobPosting are all directly applicable and all absent.
findings.recommendation: Add FinancialService schema site-wide in MainLayout with NAP, geo (27.7108334, 85.31344), areaServed and parentOrganization MV Dugar Group; then FAQPage, Article + Person, BreadcrumbList and JobPosting per page.

findings.title: FAQPage schema missing despite FAQ content already on the page
findings.description: Five question-and-answer pairs are already written and rendered on the homepage, but carry no FAQPage markup — forfeiting rich-result eligibility for zero additional content work.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the existing homepage FAQ data in FAQPage JSON-LD.

findings.title: Service data is structured in source but not marked up
findings.description: src/data/services.js already holds the five financing categories as structured objects, but /services emits no Service schema.
findings.recommendation: Emit Service schema on /services directly from the existing services.js data.

categories.name: Performance (CWV)
what_works: 18 requests total on the homepage — a lean request count
DOMContentLoaded at 865 ms and load at 866 ms on desktop
Brotli compression active; JS compresses from 663 KB to 215 KB
preconnect hints correctly present for the Google Fonts origins
Modern image formats (WebP/AVIF) already adopted

findings.title: Homepage transfers 3.79 MB
findings.description: Measured live: 3,792 KB total — 2,113 KB of images across 8 requests and 1,532 KB of fonts and CSS across 4. On a Nepali mobile connection this will very likely fail the LCP threshold.
findings.recommendation: Combine responsive image variants (2.2), route-level code splitting (2.3) and self-hosted subsetted fonts (2.4). Realistic target for images alone: 2.1 MB down to under 400 KB.

findings.title: No route-level code splitting
findings.description: A single index.js bundle means Admin.jsx — the largest file in the project at 4,868 words — plus leaflet and gsap are downloaded by every homepage visitor who never visits those pages.
findings.recommendation: Convert routes to React.lazy() with Suspense, starting with /admin, /emi-calculator and the Leaflet map component.

findings.title: Render-blocking third-party font stylesheet
findings.description: Inter and Sora are loaded via an external Google Fonts stylesheet in <head>, declaring 11 weights in total. preconnect is present, but the stylesheet still blocks render.
findings.recommendation: Self-host both families in public/fonts/ with font-display: swap, preload the two above-the-fold weights, and drop unused weights.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness
what_works: Content is well suited to passage-level citation — FAQ pairs, the 2x income-to-EMI rule, and document checklists are exactly what AI engines quote
Cloudflare Content-Signal header is present and correctly formed

findings.title: robots.txt blocks every major AI crawler
findings.description: The Cloudflare-managed robots.txt sets Disallow: / for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Bytespider, Applebot-Extended and meta-externalagent, with Content-Signal: ai-train=no. The brand cannot be cited by ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Meta AI. This is Cloudflare's default posture, very likely enabled without a deliberate decision.
findings.recommendation: Make this an explicit business decision. Recommended middle path: allow citation crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) while keeping ai-train=no. Writing your own robots.txt overrides the managed one, so the decision gets made either way.

findings.title: Client-side rendering blocks non-rendering AI crawlers
findings.description: Even if crawlers were allowed, AI crawlers that do not execute JavaScript would see a 942-byte empty shell. Both the robots policy and the rendering model must be fixed for AI visibility.
findings.recommendation: Pair the crawler-policy decision with build-time prerendering so allowed crawlers actually receive content.

findings.title: No llms.txt
findings.description: /llms.txt returns the SPA shell rather than a real file.
findings.recommendation: Add llms.txt only if AI crawler access is opened. Note that Google Search ignores it — this is a bet on emerging conventions, not a ranking factor.

categories.name: Images
what_works: Modern formats (WebP/AVIF) already in use across most assets
The 6 images that do carry alt text are descriptive and useful, e.g. 'John Deere tractor and harvesters we finance'

findings.title: Images served at up to 30x their displayed size
findings.description: A 3000x1975 photo is served and displayed at 95x600 px; another 3000x2004 image gets the same treatment. No srcset and no responsive variants — every visitor downloads full-resolution originals to fill a thin vertical strip.
findings.recommendation: Generate 400/800/1600 px variants with sharp (already a devDependency) and emit srcset + sizes.

findings.title: 6 of 12 homepage images have empty alt attributes
findings.description: wp9212100.webp, rv-4006491267651bec.avif, photo-1612057473166.avif, 70_kmph_top_speed.webp, photo-1594771804886.avif and sinharai power.jpg all render with alt="".
findings.recommendation: Add descriptive alt text to all six, matching the quality of the existing alt text.

findings.title: No width/height or lazy loading on any image
findings.description: Not one of the 12 homepage images declares width or height, making every image a CLS contributor. None uses loading="lazy", including below-fold images.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit width/height to every img, loading="lazy" and decoding="async" below the fold, and fetchpriority="high" on the hero.

findings.title: Oversized source files and non-descriptive filenames
findings.description: src/assets/images/ holds a 13 MB 'ZAXIS 140H Ultra.JPG' and an untracked 1.7 MB 'ChatGPT Image Aug 10, 2026....png'. Filenames such as photo-1612057473166-af2affdb92ad.avif carry no keyword value.
findings.recommendation: Remove both oversized files from the bundle path and rename assets descriptively, e.g. passenger-car-financing-nepal.avif.

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Add per-route titles, meta descriptions and canonicals via a React 19 Seo component (3-4 h)
Ship public/sitemap.xml and a site-owned public/robots.txt, then submit in Google Search Console (1 h)
Return real 404 status codes for unmatched paths; add noindex to NotFound as interim mitigation (1-2 h)
Port the six security headers from vercel.json to Cloudflare Transform Rules or public/_headers (1 h)
Lock down /admin with server-side authentication, plus robots disallow and noindex (varies)

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Add FinancialService, FAQPage, Organization, Article, BreadcrumbList and JobPosting JSON-LD (4-5 h)
Fix image delivery: responsive srcset, alt text, width/height, lazy loading, descriptive filenames (3-4 h)
Add route-level code splitting with React.lazy for /admin, /emi-calculator and the Leaflet map (2 h)
Self-host and subset fonts; raise hashed-asset cache TTL to one year immutable (2 h)
Decide the AI-crawler policy deliberately rather than inheriting Cloudflare's default (45 min)

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Expand the three highest-intent blog posts to 1,200-1,800 words (ongoing)
Add author attribution linked to /leadership bios, and ISO datePublished alongside BS dates (2-3 h)
Verify testimonial provenance against real Google Business Profile reviews before any Review schema (1 h)
Publish the NRB license number, full street address and business hours (1 h)
Link /reports from the main navigation or footer (15 min)
Add llms.txt if AI crawler access is opened (30 min)

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Set up Google Search Console and submit the sitemap — without it nothing here can be measured
Set up Bing Webmaster Tools, where the client-side rendering issue will surface first
Claim and complete the Google Business Profile with categories, hours, photos and a review cadence
Add CrUX/PageSpeed monitoring for real-world Core Web Vitals on Nepali mobile networks
Evaluate build-time prerendering (vite-plugin-prerender) to emit static HTML per route (1-2 weeks)
Re-audit after Phase 2 to confirm the health score moves
